Exact-prefix replay · development diagnosis

Does earlier stopping repair the ZCA posterior?

At the previously observed validation minimum, epoch 83, nominal 90% intervals cover 74.2–78.7% of physical-parameter truths and 78.9% of c truths. At epoch 200 those figures are 54.9–60.9% and 74.0%. The c median RMSE changes from 0.1697 at epoch 200 to 0.1677 at epoch 83; 0/6 marginal SBC screens are within their band at epoch 83. This is a diagnosis on reused development data, rather than independent acceptance of a selected estimator.

Nominal coverage is 90%. Lower validation loss and good point recovery are useful evidence, but neither alone certifies posterior uncertainty. The validation minimum at epoch 83 was already observed before this replay; these comparisons diagnose a development model and do not constitute independent acceptance.

What is replayed exactly

The replay uses the same 10,000 fixed noisy training observations, 100 fixed validation probes, frozen training-fitted ZCA transform, seed 9011, bounded six-target adapter, initialization, permutations, batch size 256 and 16-row final batch. Forty updates form one epoch. No fresh noise is introduced. The financial law remains Y=P(φ)+c h Z, with c∼Uniform(0.5,2) inferred jointly with five Heston parameters.

It stops after 100 epochs (4000 updates, 1m presentations), saving epochs 50/75/83/100. The learning-rate schedule retains its original 8000-update horizon; the final epoch-200 weights and evaluations are reused. Initialization and all 100 saved loss-probe records must match the original trajectory exactly before this report can render. The replay also verifies native checkpoint reloads with the same sampling seed.

flow = bf.networks.CouplingFlow(
    transform="spline", depth=6,
    subnet_kwargs={"widths": [128, 128], "dropout": 0.0},
)
lr = keras.optimizers.schedules.CosineDecay(
    initial_learning_rate=5e-4, decay_steps=8000, alpha=0.1,
)
optimizer = keras.optimizers.Adam(lr)
workflow = bf.BasicWorkflow(
    adapter=bounded_target_adapter, inference_network=flow,
    standardize=["inference_variables"], optimizer=optimizer,
)

Original fixed-probe losses with all evaluated checkpoints marked. Epoch 83 has the minimum observed validation loss; the previously reported model was epoch 200.

Dropout is explicitly zero. Whitening changes the numerical coordinates of the complete noisy quote vector; it does not add another noise source or change the posterior target.

For the market case, this comparison tests neural inference under the assumed model and likelihood; market-model adequacy is a separate question requiring predictive or residual checks.

Does the joint parameter dependence agree?

These checks use already saved neural posterior draws and existing ready joint MCMC chains. Every matrix retains all six targets. The table summarizes absolute differences across the 15 distinct off-diagonal Pearson correlations. Values near zero mean closer agreement for this linear-dependence summary. Pearson correlations do not characterize every nonlinear dependence or establish equality of full joint posteriors. MCMC draws are serially dependent; these summaries have no Monte Carlo acceptance threshold.
